source_backed_traces.trace: UnitInterval privately retains f32, rejects nonfinite and values outside inclusive[0,1], and is reused by Deserialize through TryFrom. ZERO/ONE/HALF and Default are admitted endpoints. The animation module reexports this exact core owner; new signatures do not introduce a duplicate type or raw forwarding API.
source_backed_traces.assessment: Both interpolation APIs receive the admitted owner. fraction() extraction occurs at scalar arithmetic boundaries.

source_backed_traces.contract: Speed interpolation producer to retained result
source_backed_traces.trace: Source-reference navigation and actual bodies identify two production NonnegativeSpeed.checked_lerp calls. Locomotion admits its clamped run ratio once, then copies that owner through speed/cycle/flight operations and compares with HALF. Jog speed admits the intentionally clamped smooth-endurance polynomial before its speed lerp. The speed kernel retains self+(other-self)*factor order, then calls the same nonnegative finite result admission and maps nonfinite arithmetic to Overflow.
source_backed_traces.assessment: No raw internal factor parameter, primitive round trip, duplicated retained authority, unchecked output publication or changed valid-factor arithmetic order was introduced.

source_backed_traces.contract: Cycle interpolation and remaining typed receivers
source_backed_traces.trace: CycleDelta remains a signed unwrapped finite displacement; only its interpolant becomes UnitInterval. It keeps the same native FloatExt.lerp call and from_arithmetic overflow rejection. The one current cycle caller reuses run. Bounce computes and admits the distinct complement1-run.fraction(); flight directly reuses run. HeightDistance.scaled_by extracts only for multiplication and re-admits its result. Existing ResponseShapingTime and both camera calls already use UnitInterval and stay unchanged.
source_backed_traces.assessment: The migration preserves distinct output units and existing fallibility. Finite endpoint values are not claimed to make every floating-point interpolation infallible.

source_backed_traces.contract: Endurance clamp and intentional behavior change
source_backed_traces.trace: Existing endurance clamp[0,5], branch<=1, polynomial endurance*endurance*(3-2*endurance), upper-endurance power curve and speed interpolation order remain. New clamp[0,1] applies to the computed polynomial before UnitInterval admission.
source_backed_traces.assessment: This enforces the intended unit-domain policy for finite polynomial roundoff and is deliberate. No requirement to preserve tiny prior extrapolation, prior incidental error shape or bitwise equality was imposed. No empirical/all-input floating-point equivalence claim or new tuning/YAML parameter.

source_backed_traces.trace: SpeedError derives thiserror::Error and owns FractionError via#[from], retaining a structured source and contextual Display. Existing four speed rejection messages remain explicitly declared. The sole explicit variant conversion found in source, AnimationValueError::from(SpeedError), includes Fraction(error)=>Self::from(error), reusing canonical unit-fraction classification. BattleResolutionError and CameraError retain SpeedError through existing typed variants.
source_backed_traces.assessment: No missing exhaustiveness arm, error-string branching, string erasure, compatibility shim or invented legacy source/downcast contract was found.

source_backed_traces.trace: Native-controller assignment receives SpeedResult, logs any Err and continues before assigning a bad speed. Jog-derived breath/exhaustion and ordinary-controller paths propagate typed errors. Projection checks locomotion/profile/cycle arithmetic before gait-phase/contact writes; prediction obtains profile/cycle results before phase-retention writes. Existing state updates elsewhere in these methods remain unchanged.
source_backed_traces.assessment: No new partial state commit or swallowed fraction rejection was introduced by the changed producer/API calls. This is not a claim that the complete unchanged routines are transactional under every failure.
